# AGENTS.md — engineering rules

Shared rules for every AI coding tool in this repo. Generated into each tool's native format by `forge sync` — edit this source, not the generated files. Keep lean (tools cap the combined size).

## Workflow
- Explore -> plan -> code -> verify. For multi-file or unfamiliar changes, plan first; skip planning for one-line fixes.
- Never call work done without a check you can run: tests, build exit code, lint, or a diff against expected. Show the command + output, don't just assert success.
- Fix root causes, not symptoms. Never suppress an error to make a check pass.

## Cognitive substrate (run before acting)
- Before ambiguous, expensive, multi-file, or mutating work, run `forge substrate "<task>" --json` (or call the MCP tool `substrate_check`). Check the evidence delivered by your host hook. If no evidence was delivered, call `forge_evidence` for the task or the actual failure, or run `forge evidence` with the task. For a missing capability call `forge_tool_find` with the job. Use `forge_team_plan` to split independent checks when appropriate.
- If it returns `okToProceed:false`, ask the returned `assumption.questions` before editing — do not guess an under-specified task.
- Start at the recommended `route.tier` (cheapest capable model); escalate only after an external verifier fails, never preemptively.
- Read `impact.impactedFiles` (predicted blast radius) before editing a named symbol/file, and split `scope.clusters` of independent work into separate sessions.
- Treat `memory.advisory` and minimality warnings as advisory; tests, graph membership, and human corrections always override the model.
- Run `verification.checklist` and show the output before claiming done.

## End-to-end completeness
- A change is DONE only when code, tests, docs, and session state moved together: run `forge docs sync` to sweep the diff for stale doc mentions, and `forge handoff "<done>" --next "<next>"` before stopping. A Stop gate enforces this floor — code moved with nothing following blocks once, with the repair checklist.
- Never assume silently: answer preflight's clarifying questions, or proceed knowing the assumption is RECORDED to the session log and resurfaces in the handoff — verify it before claiming done.
- Record non-obvious choices with `forge decide "<decision> — <reason>"`; read `.forge/decisions.md` (or bare `forge decide`) before re-deciding anything a past session settled.

## Reuse & dependencies
- Reuse an existing util/component/pattern before writing new; the smallest change that fits wins.
- Before adding a dependency, verify the current best option from live sources (docs, GitHub health) — prefer what the project already uses.
- Only build from scratch when reuse genuinely doesn't fit, and say why.

## Code style
- Match the surrounding file's conventions over any personal default.
- Comment the non-obvious "why", never restate the "what".
- Guard array/object access; wrap fallible async in try/catch; handle errors explicitly (no empty catch).
- Keep functions small and single-purpose; separate pure logic from I/O so it's testable.

## Testing
- Write tests with the code. For a bug fix, write the failing test first, then fix.
- Cover the edge cases the task names: empty, error, boundary. Prefer real inputs over heavy mocking.
- Run the suite + typecheck + lint and show the output before claiming done.

## Security
- Never write secrets, tokens, or keys into code or commits. `.env*` and key files are guard-protected — don't work around it.
- Validate and sanitize input at trust boundaries; use parameterized queries, never string-concatenated SQL.
- Check paths for traversal before file operations; prefer HTTPS for external requests.

## Production standards (2026)
- Validate at trust boundaries with a schema (e.g. Zod): parse untrusted input (API, env, file, LLM output) into typed values before use — never trust it raw.
- Keep business logic in use-cases/domain, not controllers; hide the DB/ORM behind a repository interface; return DTOs, never raw DB models.
- Check ownership/authorization on every object access (OWASP API #1 — never trust a user-supplied ID); paginate every list; make retried mutations idempotent.
- Use a typed error model: typed codes, safe public messages, internal detail logged with a requestId. Never swallow errors or leak stack traces to clients.
- Emit structured logs (level, message, requestId, service, durationMs); for services add metrics/traces (OpenTelemetry) and track error rate, p95 latency, and AI token cost.
- Treat AI/LLM output as untrusted (OWASP LLM Top 10): verify it, never execute it directly, never put secrets/PII in prompts, give agent tools least privilege + human approval for destructive actions.
- Prefer boring, typed, maintained tech; contract-first APIs (OpenAPI 3.1) with a new version for every breaking change; don't over-pattern simple code.

## Git
- Conventional commits: `type(scope): description` (feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf).
- Stage specific files, not `git add .`. Never force-push shared branches.
- Ask before: push, commit, PR merge, history rewrite, `rm -rf`, dropping DB tables, or touching production.

## UI
- Build and check mobile AND desktop. Include clear loading/empty/error states; avoid layout shift.
- Follow DESIGN.md if present; keep one visual direction per project.

## AI interfaces & design quality
- Commit to an aesthetic before coding; avoid AI-slop defaults (Inter/Roboto/Arial/system fonts, purple-gradient-on-white, generic card grids). Pick 2–3 typefaces and a 4–6 color palette with semantic roles.
- Meet WCAG: body text ≥4.5:1 contrast (large/UI ≥3:1), visible :focus-visible on every interactive element, tap targets ≥24×24px, alt text + form labels, and wrap animations ≥200ms in prefers-reduced-motion.
- Empty states are never dead ends: show a plain-language message + a clear next step. Error messages name the field, explain the problem, and suggest a fix — never 'Something went wrong'.
- For AI-driven UIs: show concise rationale, assumptions, tool actions, sources, verification evidence, and uncertainty — without exposing private hidden reasoning traces. Give live preview/feedback over blind prompting, and provide fallback paths when the model fails.
- Pick the interaction pattern deliberately — a co-editing canvas or inline controls beat a wall-of-text chatbot when the user is steering structured output.
- When AI audits a UI, only ASSERT the deterministic (contrast math, missing focus ring/alt/label) — keep hierarchy/taste/pattern-fit advisory so the audit doesn't hallucinate false positives.

## Agent orchestration
- Start long commands (test suites, builds, e2e runs) in the background and wait for the completion signal. Never write sleep or poll loops; read results with `tail`/`grep`, not by re-reading whole logs. `[orch.no-polling]`
- Run at most 2 agents in parallel, and never more than the scarcest shared resource (test environment, ports, database, CI runners) can serve at once. Queue the rest. `[orch.parallel-cap]`
- Use sub-agents only when the work splits into independent parts that together exceed one context window. Otherwise one agent does it; most coding has few parallel parts. `[orch.multi-agent-gate]`
- Split by independent angle, one sub-agent each, started together within the parallel cap. Each brief names the objective, output format, tools and sources, and what is out of bounds. `[orch.split-by-angle]`
- Size effort to the question: a fact is one agent and a few tool calls, a comparison two to four sub-agents, deep work more. Never more agents than angles. `[orch.scale-effort]`
- Run full e2e and integration suites in CI. Locally, run only fast checks (typecheck, lint, unit tests of the code you touched) before pushing. `[orch.ci-heavy-checks]`
- Give each sub-agent one small task and a fresh context. It writes findings to a file and hands back the path and a short report (changes, checks, open items). `[orch.fresh-subagents]`
- Pick each agent's model with `forge route "<task>" --json` (add `--mode unattended` for agents nobody watches). Never start at the top tier by default. `[orch.route-models]`
- Changes touching money, auth, secrets, migrations or security ship with tests in the same change and a lead review of the diff. UI-only tests may follow later. `[orch.risk-review]`
- If local e2e is unavoidable, serialise it behind a lock or give each agent its own ports and database. `[orch.isolated-env]`
- As lead, keep replies to completion notifications short and do not re-read large files or logs; read the sub-agent's report. `[orch.lean-lead]`

## Working method
- Before solving, check two things: is the goal right, and do you have what it needs (context, tools, access)? Fix the missing one first. `[method.goal-and-means]`
- Act on what you checked, not on what you assume. Check a claim's source (a log, a payload, another agent's report) before you rely on it. `[method.evidence-first]`
- Watch for three traps: doing it because it was always done, picking the easy fix and calling it right, and acting on an untested assumption. `[method.thinking-traps]`
- When choosing between options, list them, strike any that breaks a hard limit (harm, the contract, the evidence), then rank the rest by benefit, certainty and cost. `[method.rule-out-then-rank]`
- When something breaks, read the log and the inputs first, then change one thing at a time until the cause is isolated (bisect, do not guess). `[method.isolate]`
- After each action (an edit, a command, a click), check that the state actually changed. If it did not, choose a different action instead of repeating it. `[method.confirm-effect]`
- Done needs reproducible proof: a check that failed before and passes now. "It should work" is not done. `[method.proof-of-done]`
- Test the smallest cases: empty, zero, null, boundaries, off-by-one, time zones, leap days, Unicode and right-to-left text. `[method.smallest-cases]`
- Write the agreement before the work: scope, acceptance criteria, interfaces. Ambiguity left unwritten becomes a dispute later. `[method.write-it-down]`
- Never reach green by breaking a rule or a user: no disabled tests, skipped hooks, hard-coded secrets, force-pushes or silent contract changes. `[method.no-harmful-shortcut]`
- Do not fix one harm by causing another: keep public contracts stable, keep security fixes minimal, and phase a breaking change (warn, support both, then remove). `[method.fix-without-breaking]`
- For a high-stakes or deadlocked choice, get an independent review. To settle a conflict between agents or requirements, weigh both sides' evidence and aim to reconcile, not to win. `[method.consult]`
- Do the clear, mechanical steps with plain code or a tool; spend model reasoning on the parts that are truly ambiguous. `[method.plain-code-first]`
- When the context cannot support an answer, say so and name what is missing instead of guessing. `[method.say-what-is-missing]`
- Hand work on with pointers, not retold summaries: file and line, a commit or a hash, so the next agent checks the original. `[method.pointers-not-summaries]`
- When a decision changes, replace the old fact and keep it only in history. Never leave two conflicting versions in active notes. `[method.supersede-stale]`
- Once a plan is tested, carry it out without endless polishing, then record the result and the lesson. `[method.finish]`
